title: A Rearmed Germany's Place in Europe
gist: Germany is rearming at a pace far above other European NATO members, enabled by a constitutional change allowing debt-funded defense and pushing its defense budget to a 36-year high, but the far-right AfD's 44% first-place finish in eastern state elections shows the domestic consensus behind this role is under strain.

insights.claim: Germany changed its constitution to allow debt funding for defense spending, published its first military strategy, and has raised its defense budget to a 36-year high.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Structural, debt-financed German defense demand supports European defense contractors and Bund supply.

insights.claim: Germany's rearmament is driven by the United States pulling back from Europe and heightened threats of Russian aggression, ending decades of military restraint.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: US retrenchment is a durable tailwind for European defense spending independent of any single budget cycle.

insights.claim: On September 6 the far-right Alternative for Germany party took first place in state elections in eastern Germany with 44 percent of the vote.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Rising AfD strength is a political risk to the durability of Germany's debt-funded rearmament and Europe-leadership role.

insights.claim: Germany is being asked to take a much larger role in European security just as the post-war political consensus underpinning its foreign policy comes under growing strain.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Watch German domestic politics as a key variable for European security policy continuity.
insights.quote: Germany is therefore being asked to assume a much larger role in European security while the political consensus that has underpinned its post-war foreign policy is coming under growing strain.
